title: Multimodal deep learning system supports early diagnosis of biliary atresia
summary: A deep learning model on ultrasound images, clinical data and laboratory results from 1579 participants reached an AUC of 0.9870 on an internal test set, and a simplified blood-free model reached 0.9799. In a prospective external test set of 171 cases the multimodal model reached 0.9740, comparable to a radiologist with over 10 years of experience (0.9766). AI assistance raised less experienced radiologists' AUC from 0.6667 to 0.9006.
ai_technology: Multimodal deep learning model on ultrasound images, clinical and laboratory data, plus a simplified blood-free version

evidence.tested: Retrospective training and internal testing, and a prospective external test set of 171 cases, with comparison against human experts.
evidence.unknown: Performance in other populations and effect on timing of surgery; full text not reviewed.
evidence.ai_role: Classifies infants as biliary atresia or not from combined ultrasound and clinical data.
